bug_semantics: When STOMP auto-create is enabled, an authenticated principal holding only SEND or CONSUME permission can request an unsupported routing type in a SEND destination-type or SUBSCRIBE subscription-type header. The vulnerable STOMP path sees the existing address, copies its routing-type set, adds the requested type, and calls ActiveMQServer.updateAddressInfo directly, bypassing the ServerSession CREATE_ADDRESS security check. Because checkRoutingSemantics runs only after this mutation, it sees the newly added type and accepts the operation. The result is an unauthorized persistent augmentation of the address routing semantics.
flaw_origin: Commit d773e8f66b5db2b0fcaa646384c24690d38aaa69 intentionally added support for STOMP clients to use the same address with different routing types. Its new existing-address branch performed the update through manager.getServer().updateAddressInfo rather than the authorization-enforcing ServerSession API, creating the root authorization bypass.
ai_marker: None. `git cat-file commit d773e8f66b5db2b0fcaa646384c24690d38aaa69` shows author Justin Bertram <jbertram@apache.org>, committer Clebert Suconic <clebertsuconic@apache.org>, the subject `ARTEMIS-1794 STOMP clients using same addr w/diff routing types`, an empty body, and no Co-Authored-By, Generated-with, AI, or bot marker. The BIC is an ordinary one-parent human commit from 2018.
evidence: The Apache oss-security announcement at https://www.openwall.com/lists/oss-security/2026/05/27/8 identifies ARTEMIS-5996/CVE-2026-40914, describes unauthorized routing-type augmentation by a STOMP user with only send or consume permission, declares 2.0.0-2.44.0 and 2.50.0-2.53.0 affected, and recommends 2.54.0.

`git show d773e8f66b5db2b0fcaa646384c24690d38aaa69 -- artemis-protocols/artemis-stomp-protocol/src/main/java/org/apache/activemq/artemis/core/protocol/stomp/StompConnection.java` shows the first existing-address branch: when the requested type is absent and auto-create-addresses is enabled, it copies existing types, adds the requested type, and invokes `manager.getServer().updateAddressInfo(simpleQueue, routingTypes)`. The same commit's tests explicitly say a STOMP send should alter an existing address to support the second routing type.

At the BIC, `git grep -n -E 'autoCreateDestinationIfPossible|checkRoutingSemantics' d773e8f66b5db2b0fcaa646384c24690d38aaa69 -- .../StompConnection.java .../VersionedStompFrameHandler.java` shows mutation before validation on both paths: subscribe lines 692/694 and send lines 190/192 call autoCreateDestinationIfPossible before checkRoutingSemantics.

Direct parent verification: `git show e937c9903f9fa429c23fe50a3fd49e99ad2de0b9:artemis-protocols/artemis-stomp-protocol/src/main/java/org/apache/activemq/artemis/core/protocol/stomp/StompConnection.java` shows autoCreateDestinationIfPossible acts only when getAddressInfo is null, creates through `session.createAddress`, and contains no existing-address routing-set update. Its subsequent checkRoutingSemantics rejects a requested type absent from an existing address.

Independent origin checks agree: `git log 53173375c4d5e4b57890e89d37ed8b666c974474^ -L '/public void autoCreateDestinationIfPossible/,/^   }/':artemis-protocols/artemis-stomp-protocol/src/main/java/org/apache/activemq/artemis/core/protocol/stomp/StompConnection.java` traces the vulnerable branch to d773e8f66b5db2b0fcaa646384c24690d38aaa69; `git log --all --reverse -S'manager.getServer().updateAddressInfo(simpleQueue, routingTypes)' -- .../StompConnection.java` returns d773e8f66b5db2b0fcaa646384c24690d38aaa69 as the addition and ede2051960ddd6bf5657076fe5889f18a5699c6c only as a later refactor/removal of that spelling.

Release introduction: tag 2.5.0 resolves to 5f5b1dcf8f731b53d1b271fdde46dddacdd71bd7 and has no `updateAddressInfo(simpleQueue, routingTypes)` hit; tag 2.6.0 resolves to bcaa11c2eea681d5758398be0b8c2ff8ae2c2878 and contains it at StompConnection.java:297. `git tag --contains d773e8f66b5db2b0fcaa646384c24690d38aaa69` begins at 2.6.0 and includes every existing release tag through 2.44.0 and then 2.50.0 onward. Thus direct history narrows the exact mechanism's effective floor to 2.6.0, despite the advisory's conservative 2.0.0 floor; no 2.45.0-2.49.0 tags exist.

Closing fix: `git show 53173375c4d5e4b57890e89d37ed8b666c974474` deletes the duplicated direct update and changes both SEND and SUBSCRIBE to StompConnection.checkAutoCreate, which calls `getSession().getCoreSession().checkAutoCreate(QueueConfiguration...)`. In tag 2.54.0, ServerSessionImpl.checkAutoCreate updates an existing address by calling ServerSessionImpl.createAddress, whose line `securityCheck(art.getName(), CheckType.CREATE_ADDRESS, this)` enforces the missing permission.

Fix boundary: `git grep -n -E 'updateAddressInfo\(simpleDestination|checkAutoCreate\(destination' 2.53.0 -- .../StompConnection.java .../VersionedStompFrameHandler.java` finds the vulnerable direct update at StompConnection.java:197. The same command at 2.54.0 finds checkAutoCreate at StompConnection.java:491 and VersionedStompFrameHandler.java:196 and no direct update. `git tag --contains 53173375c4d5e4b57890e89d37ed8b666c974474` returns 2.54.0, 2.55.0, and 2.56.0, making 2.54.0 the first fixed release.

`git cat-file commit d773e8f66b5db2b0fcaa646384c24690d38aaa69` directly verifies the full parent e937c9903f9fa429c23fe50a3fd49e99ad2de0b9, human author/committer identities, 2018 timestamps, and complete absence of AI trailers or bot identity. The commit has one parent and is the narrow ARTEMIS-1794 implementation, not a merge, release/backport, revert, move, or squash aggregate.
reasoning: The vulnerability is caused by the newly added direct server update, not by later renames or refactors. The parent cannot mutate an existing address and instead rejects a mismatched requested routing type, while d773e8f66b5db2b0fcaa646384c24690d38aaa69 adds exactly the mutation that makes the later semantic check self-satisfying. The direct fix 53173375c4d5e4b57890e89d37ed8b666c974474 removes that bypass and delegates to a session path that checks CREATE_ADDRESS. Tag and source checks establish introduction in 2.6.0, persistence through 2.53.0, and closure in 2.54.0; the published lower bound of 2.0.0 is broader than the exact code history. AI attribution is judged solely from the BIC object. It contains only named human identities and no AI/bot marker, so reporter credit to bugbunny.ai and any properties of the 2026 fix are irrelevant and the correct verdict is NOT_AI.
